claims.claim: Google released SynthID Detector so the public can identify whether text, image, audio, or video was created with AI.

claims.claim: Google says it has applied imperceptible watermarks to more than 180 billion images and videos and 240,000 years of audio.

claims.supporting_quote: The technology relies on imperceptible watermarks that Google has already applied to more than 180 billion images and videos, alongside 240,000 years of audio content.

claims.claim: SynthID Detector is available through Google DeepMind and currently works on media from Google, OpenAI, Nvidia, Kakao, and Apple.

claims.source_title: Google releases new AI detection tool – how it works

claims.claim: The watermarks remain detectable after cropping or filters without altering quality for human users.
claims.episode_span: Marks are meant to stay readable after a crop or a filter, without changing what a person sees or hears.
claims.source_title: Google releases new AI detection tool – how it works
claims.supporting_quote: The invisible watermarks remain detectable even after media is cropped or modified with filters, without altering the quality for human users.

claims.claim: The launch aligns with the EU AI Act requirement that generative AI outputs be identifiable to automated systems.

claims.supporting_quote: The launch aligns with the European Union 's AI Act, which requires generative AI platforms to make their outputs identifiable to automated systems.
